in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'idus', which is the past participle of the verb 'ideo', meaning 'to know' or 'to see'; a name given to individuals who were known or recognized by others.

in_english.name: Id

data.cultural_impact: The name Id is most notably associated with Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus' twelve apostles who infamously betrayed Him. At the Last Supper, Judas agreed to betray Jesus to the religious authorities for thirty pieces of silver. Although there is no clear biblical reference to Judas having this name before the betrayal, a later tradition in Western Christianity adopted the name 'Judas Iscariot' due to its association with betrayal and deceit.
data.spiritual_significance: Id serves as a stark reminder of the human capacity for deceit and sin. It challenges us to strive for honesty and faithfulness in all areas of life. Judas' tragic story encourages us to reflect on the consequences of our actions and to remain true to our commitments - especially to our spiritual paths.
